title: An overview of Tableau, Looker, Metabase and Streamlit

videos.script: Every BI tool draws a bar chart. So comparing them by features tells you very little. {{bars}} Two questions tell them apart. Who builds? And where do the definitions live? {{axes}} Tableau puts an analyst in front of a canvas. Looker makes a modeller describe everything first, in files. {{commercial}} Those two are commercial, and this course does not run them. It shows how they think. {{think}} Metabase and Streamlit sit at opposite corners, and both run on your machine. In Metabase, anybody builds through menus. {{metabase}} In Streamlit, a short program is the whole app. {{streamlit}} You will ask Metabase a question that needs a join it was never told about. Then you will run a Streamlit app, part by part. {{app}} And the same revenue figure will arrive through three different tools. Because none of them was allowed to decide what revenue means. {{end}}
